before_objects.title: Observer decomposition of a symmetric stress-energy tensor
before_objects.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, $\Omega\subseteq A$ open, and let $T$ be a continuous symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest projection $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ and $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c). At a point $p\in\Omega$ define $\varepsilon:=T^{ab}n_an_b$, $\pi^a:=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$ and $S^{ab}:=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$. Then: (a) $\pi$ lies in $n^\perp$, $S$ is symmetric and horizontal in both slots ($S^{ab}n_b=n_aS^{ab}=0$), and $$T^{ab}=\varepsilon\,n^an^b+c\,(n^a\pi^b+\pi^an^b)+S^{ab}.$$ (b) Contracting with $n$ gives $T^{ab}n_b=-\varepsilon n^a-c\pi^a$; hence $\varepsilon$ and $\pi$ are determined by $T$ and $n$, and the decomposition is unique among decompositions $T^{ab}=\varepsilon' n^an^b+c(n^a\pi'^b+\pi'^an^b)+S'^{ab}$ with $\pi'\in n^\perp$ and $S'$ symmetric horizontal: $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon$, $\pi'=\pi$, $S'=S$. (c) In the model's physical reading with $U=cn$, $\varepsilon$ is the energy density (joule per cubic metre) and $\pi$ the momentum density (kilogram per square metre per second) measured by the observer $U$, the mathematical content asserted here is the identity in (a) and the uniqueness in (b) alone. No choice principle is used.
before_objects.strategy: Pointwise linear algebra. Since $h$ is the projection of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) with image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\operatorname{span}(n)$, and $\delta^a{}_c=h^a{}_c-n^an_c$, expand $T^{ab}=(h^a{}_c-n^an_c)(h^b{}_d-n^bn_d)T^{cd}$ and use symmetry of $T$ to obtain (a) with the stated signs. For (b), contract (a) with $n_b$ using $n_bn^b=-1$, $n_b\pi^b=0$ and $S^{ab}n_b=0$; uniqueness follows by contracting a general decomposition with $n_an_b$ (gives $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon$), with $h_{ac}h_{bd}$ (gives $S'=S$), and with $n_b$ (gives $\pi'=\pi$). No choice principle is used.

before_objects.title: Dust: conservation of rho n tensor n is equivalent to continuity and inertial flow
before_objects.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $\rho:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$ with $\rho>0$, let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ field with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ everywhere (a future unit timelike field, [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)), and set $T^{ab}:=\rho\,n^an^b$ (a $C^1$ symmetric $(2,0)$ field). Then, on $\Omega$, (a) $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ if and only if both $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ (continuity) and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ (inertial flow); (b) if $\rho\ge0$ is allowed to vanish, the implication $\partial_aT^{ab}=0\Rightarrow n^a\partial_an^b=0$ is asserted only on the open set $\{\rho>0\}$, and no assertion is made where $\rho=0$; (c) if $x:J\to A$ is a $C^2$ curve with $x'(s)=n(x(s))$ for all $s$ (an integral curve of $n$), then $x''(s)=0$: the flow lines of an inertial unit field are affine straight lines in the affine structure of $A$. The lemma is the exact mathematical content of the dust equations; it asserts no matter model, no interaction and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used.
before_objects.strategy: Expand $\partial_aT^{ab}=(\partial_a\rho)n^an^b+\rho(\partial_an^a)n^b+\rho n^a\partial_an^b$ and rewrite the first two terms as $(\partial_a(\rho n^a))n^b+\rho n^a\partial_an^b$. Contract with $n_b$ and use $n_bn^b=-1$, $n_b\partial_an^b=\tfrac12\partial_a(n_bn^b)=0$ to obtain $n_b\partial_aT^{ab}=-\partial_a(\rho n^a)$. Hence conservation gives continuity, and then the remaining horizontal part gives $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the converse is immediate. For (c), differentiate: $x''(s)=n^a\partial_an^b(x(s))=0$ by the chain rule, so $x'$ is constant and $x$ is affine. Source: the equivalence is the flat restriction of the dust computation of G6 and of the dust equations read off from (4.53)-(4.55) of Tong; the positivity hypothesis is stated because the converse needs it. No choice principle is used.

before_objects.title: Perfect fluid: conservation is equivalent to the energy and Euler equations
before_objects.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $\varepsilon,P:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) and set $T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$. Write $D\varepsilon:=n^a\partial_a\varepsilon$, $\vartheta:=\partial_an^a$, $a^b:=n^a\partial_an^b$ and $h^{bc}:=\eta^{bc}+n^bn^c$ (the expansion scalar, acceleration and rest projector of [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] for the congruence $n$ and the flat derivative of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]). Then the identity $$\partial_aT^{ab}=n^b\big(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta\big)+\big((\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP\big)$$ holds on $\Omega$, and consequently $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$ if and only if $D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta=0$ and $(\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP=0$ on $\Omega$. The two equations are the energy-balance and Euler equations of the model; the lemma asserts no equation of state, no thermodynamic relation and no causality condition. No choice principle is used.
before_objects.strategy: Compute $\partial_aT^{ab}=\partial_a[(\varepsilon+P)n^a]n^b+(\varepsilon+P)n^a\partial_an^b+\partial^bP$, rewrite $\partial_a[(\varepsilon+P)n^a]=D\varepsilon+DP+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta$ with $DP=n^a\partial_aP$, and decompose $\partial^bP=h^{bc}\partial_cP-n^bDP$ because $\eta^{bc}=h^{bc}-n^bn^c$; the terms in $DP$ cancel, leaving the displayed identity. Contracting with $n_b$ gives $-\big(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta\big)$ and projecting with $h$ gives the second bracket, so the two equations are equivalent to conservation. Source: the flat restriction of the perfect-fluid computation of G6 and of (4.53)-(4.55) of Tong. No choice principle is used.

before_objects.title: Dust stress-energy in a boosted inertial frame
before_objects.statement: In an inertial frame $x$ let dust at rest have rest energy density $\rho>0$, so $T^{ab}=\rho\,\delta^a_0\delta^b_0$; the only nonzero component is $T^{00}=\rho$. Consider the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along the $x^1$ axis with parameter $\beta$, $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$: $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$, $x'^2=x^2$, $x'^3=x^3$. By the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii), $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2\beta\rho,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2\beta^2\rho,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=0,$$ all remaining components zero; equivalently $T'=\rho\,n'\otimes n'$ where $n'$ is the image of $e_0$ under the boost, $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$, the future unit direction of the dust in the primed frame. The primed energy density $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho$ carries one factor of $\gamma$ from the increased energy of each dust particle and one from the contracted volume, as in the source computation. All primed components are constant, so $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=0$, consistently with [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. The example is a component computation; it asserts no measurement and no dynamics.
before_objects.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ with the boost matrix $\Lambda$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: only $T^{00}=\rho$ contributes, giving the displayed components; the identification $T'=\rho n'\otimes n'$ follows from $n'=\Lambda e_0$. Constancy and conservation are immediate. Source: Crowell Example 5 p. 185 and (1.106) of Carroll. No choice principle is used.

before_objects.title: Perfect fluid components in its rest frame and in a moving frame
before_objects.statement: Let $T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$ be the perfect-fluid tensor of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]], with $n$ future unit. In an inertial frame with $n=e_0$ (fluid at rest) the components are $T^{00}=\varepsilon$, $T^{11}=T^{22}=T^{33}=P$ and all other components zero. Under the passive boost along $x^1$ with parameter $\beta$ (so that in the primed frame the fluid moves with speed $v=\beta c$ in the negative $x'^1$ direction), the component law gives $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta^2+P,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=P,$$ all remaining components zero. In particular the observer at rest in the primed frame measures the energy density $T'(e_0',e_0')=T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P$, which differs from the rest-frame density $\varepsilon$ unless $\beta=0$ and is at least $\varepsilon$ when $\varepsilon+P\ge0$; the transverse diagonal components stay equal to the pressure $P$. The computation uses the observer decomposition of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] to read $T'^{00}$ as an energy density; it asserts no equation of state and no measurement.
before_objects.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d[(\varepsilon+P)n^cn^d+P\eta^{cd}]$ using $\eta'=\eta$ (metric preservation, [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]]) and $n'=\Lambda n$ with $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$; the displayed components follow. The energy-density reading is clause (c) of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] at $n=e_0'$. Source: (4.53) of Tong, (1.107)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.6 of Crowell. No choice principle is used.

before_objects.title: A dust solution with constant velocity and transverse density profile
before_objects.statement: Let $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let $n$ be the constant field with inertial components $n^0=\gamma$, $n^1=\gamma\beta$, $n^2=n^3=0$ (so $\eta(n,n)=-1$), and let $\rho(t,x)=\rho_0(x^2,x^3)$ be a positive $C^1$ function of the transverse coordinates only. Then $n^a\partial_a\rho=\gamma(\partial_0\rho+\beta\partial_1\rho)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ because $n$ is constant, so $(\rho,n)$ satisfies the dust equations and $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$ is conserved by [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. If $\rho_0$ is supported in the spatial box $\bar K=[c_1,d_1]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$, the slice integrals $Q^b(s)=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ satisfy $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ for all $s_1<s_2$ by [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(c), since $T$ is time-independent and its spatial side flux through the faces of $\bar K$ vanishes. The flow lines are the parallel straight lines $x^1=\beta x^0+\mathrm{const}$, $x^2,x^3$ constant. The example exhibits a family of exact solutions of the dust equations; it asserts no interaction and no measurement.
before_objects.strategy: Verify $\eta(n,n)=-\gamma^2+\gamma^2\beta^2=-\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=-1$ and both dust equations as displayed; conservation and the slice constancy follow from [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]] and [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(c) applied on a slab whose spatial box contains $\operatorname{supp}\rho_0$. This is an explicit computation in the page's framework. No choice principle is used.

before_objects.title: A static uniaxial stress: tension must be constant along the stressed direction
before_objects.statement: In an inertial chart let $T^{ab}(x)=\rho(x^1)e_0^ae_0^b+P(x^1)e_1^ae_1^b$ with $\rho,P$ of class $C^1$ on an interval of $x^1$ (a static uniaxial stress field in the $e_1$ direction; $P<0$ is a tension). Then the balance components are $\partial_aT^{a0}=\partial_1T^{10}=0$ and $\partial_aT^{a1}=\partial_1T^{11}=P'(x^1)$, so $T$ is conserved on a connected chart domain if and only if $P$ is constant there; the energy density $\rho(x^1)$ may vary while the tension must be uniform along the stressed direction. This reproduces the static equilibrium condition of a uniform rope under tension and shows that conservation constrains the stress, not the energy density, in this configuration. The example is a component computation and asserts no material model.
before_objects.strategy: Compute $\partial_aT^{ab}$ directly from the displayed components: the only nonzero derivatives are $\partial_1(\rho e_0\otimes e_0)=0$ and $\partial_1(P e_1\otimes e_1)=P'(x^1)e_1\otimes e_1$; hence conservation is equivalent to $P'=0$. Source: Crowell Example 8 pp. 188-189 (rope under tension; the constant-tension condition), read with the framework's $(-,+,+,+)$ sign conventions. No choice principle is used.

before_objects.title: Null plane-wave scalar field and its conserved stress-energy tensor
before_objects.statement: Let $k\neq0$ be a null covector, $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$, with $k^\sharp$ future, let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$, and let $\varphi(x):=f(k_ax^a+\theta_0)$ in an inertial chart; take $V\equiv0$ and $K>0$. Then $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field, $\partial_a\varphi=f'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)k_a$ and $\Box\varphi=k^ak_af''(k_ax^a+\theta_0)=0$, so $\varphi$ solves the massless scalar-field equation of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]. Its Hilbert stress-energy tensor is $$T^{ab}=Kf'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)^2\,k^ak^b,$$ symmetric, future-null directed, with $T^{ab}n_an_b=Kf'^2\,(k_an^a)^2\ge0$ for every future unit observer $n$, and conserved, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, by [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solution $\Box\varphi=0$. In an inertial frame $T^{00}=Kf'^2(k^0)^2\ge0$. The example is an explicit conditional computation for the massless scalar model; it asserts no wave observation and no measurement.
before_objects.strategy: Substitute $\partial_a\varphi=f'k_a$ into the Hilbert tensor formula of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]; the potential term drops and $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$ kills the trace term, leaving $Kf'^2k^ak^b$. The equation of motion holds because $k$ is null, and conservation follows from [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]]. Source: the scalar stress tensor (4.51) of Tong with V=0; the null-covector condition is the framework's own. No choice principle is used.

proposed_subjects.title: Observer decomposition of a symmetric stress-energy tensor
proposed_subjects.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, $\Omega\subseteq A$ open, and let $T$ be a continuous symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest projection $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ and $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c). At a point $p\in\Omega$ define $\varepsilon:=T^{ab}n_an_b$, $\pi^a:=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$ and $S^{ab}:=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$. Then: (a) $\pi$ lies in $n^\perp$, $S$ is symmetric and horizontal in both slots ($S^{ab}n_b=n_aS^{ab}=0$), and $$T^{ab}=\varepsilon\,n^an^b+c\,(n^a\pi^b+\pi^an^b)+S^{ab}.$$ (b) Contracting with $n$ gives $T^{ab}n_b=-\varepsilon n^a-c\pi^a$; hence $\varepsilon$ and $\pi$ are determined by $T$ and $n$, and the decomposition is unique among decompositions $T^{ab}=\varepsilon' n^an^b+c(n^a\pi'^b+\pi'^an^b)+S'^{ab}$ with $\pi'\in n^\perp$ and $S'$ symmetric horizontal: $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon$, $\pi'=\pi$, $S'=S$. (c) In any adapted inertial orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$, the numerical components of this decomposition are $\varepsilon=T^{00}$, $\pi^0=0$, $\pi^i=T^{0i}/c$ and $S^{0a}=S^{a0}=0$, $S^{ij}=T^{ij}$ for $i,j=1,2,3$. Define isotropic rest stress to mean $S^{ab}=p h^{ab}$ for a real scalar $p$, where $h^{ab}:=\eta^{ab}+n^an^b$. Thus $S=0$ means vanishing rest stress, and is the isotropic case $p=0$; isotropy permits any $p$, including nonzero pressure or tension. These are numerical tensor identities. Physical adoption of the energy/momentum-density reading is a separate model premise; this mathematical lemma asserts no observer measurement. No choice principle is used.

proposed_subjects.title: Dust: conservation of rho n tensor n is equivalent to continuity and inertial flow
proposed_subjects.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $\rho:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$ with $\rho>0$, let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ field which is future timelike and satisfies $\eta(n,n)=-1$ everywhere (a future unit timelike field, [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)), and set $T^{ab}:=\rho\,n^an^b$ (a $C^1$ symmetric $(2,0)$ field). Then, on $\Omega$, (a) $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ if and only if both $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ (continuity) and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ (inertial flow); (b) if $\rho\ge0$ is allowed to vanish, the implication $\partial_aT^{ab}=0\Rightarrow n^a\partial_an^b=0$ is asserted only on the open set $\{\rho>0\}$, and no assertion is made where $\rho=0$; (c) Under the conservation hypothesis $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ in (a), if $J$ is an interval and $x:J\to\Omega$ is a $C^2$ curve with $x'(s)=n(x(s))$ for all $s$ (an integral curve of $n$), then $x''(s)=0$: the flow lines of an inertial unit field are affine straight lines in the affine structure of $A$. For the nonnegative-density branch in (b), the same conclusion holds for an integral curve whose image lies in $\{\rho>0\}$, under conservation there. The lemma is the exact mathematical content of the dust equations; it asserts no matter model, no interaction and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used.
proposed_subjects.strategy: Expand $\partial_aT^{ab}=(\partial_a\rho)n^an^b+\rho(\partial_an^a)n^b+\rho n^a\partial_an^b$ and rewrite the first two terms as $(\partial_a(\rho n^a))n^b+\rho n^a\partial_an^b$. Contract with $n_b$ and use $n_bn^b=-1$, $n_b\partial_an^b=\tfrac12\partial_a(n_bn^b)=0$ to obtain $n_b\partial_aT^{ab}=-\partial_a(\rho n^a)$. Hence conservation gives continuity, and then the remaining horizontal part gives $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the converse is immediate. For (b), the same contraction gives continuity without dividing by $\rho$; the remaining term is $\rho n^a\partial_an^b=0$, so division is justified exactly where $\rho>0$. For (c), use the conservation antecedent to obtain inertial flow from (a), then differentiate: $x''(s)=n^a\partial_an^b(x(s))=0$ by the chain rule, so $x'$ is constant and $x$ is affine. Source: the equivalence is the flat restriction of the dust computation of G6 and of the dust equations read off from (4.53)-(4.55) of Tong; the positivity hypothesis is stated because the converse needs it. No choice principle is used.

proposed_subjects.title: Perfect fluid: conservation is equivalent to the energy and Euler equations
proposed_subjects.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $\varepsilon,P:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) and set $T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$. Write $D\varepsilon:=n^a\partial_a\varepsilon$, $\vartheta:=\partial_an^a$, $a^b:=n^a\partial_an^b$ and $h^{bc}:=\eta^{bc}+n^bn^c$ (these formulas define the first-order expansion scalar, acceleration and raised rest projection for the stipulated $C^1$ field; they agree with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] and [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] when the field is smooth). Then the identity $$\partial_aT^{ab}=n^b\big(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta\big)+\big((\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP\big)$$ holds on $\Omega$, and consequently $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$ if and only if $D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta=0$ and $(\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP=0$ on $\Omega$. The two equations are the energy-balance and Euler equations of the model; the lemma asserts no equation of state, no thermodynamic relation and no causality condition. No choice principle is used.
proposed_subjects.strategy: Compute $\partial_aT^{ab}=\partial_a[(\varepsilon+P)n^a]n^b+(\varepsilon+P)n^a\partial_an^b+\partial^bP$, rewrite $\partial_a[(\varepsilon+P)n^a]=D\varepsilon+DP+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta$ with $DP=n^a\partial_aP$, and decompose $\partial^bP=h^{bc}\partial_cP-n^bDP$ because $\eta^{bc}=h^{bc}-n^bn^c$; the terms in $DP$ cancel, leaving the displayed identity. The second bracket is horizontal: $n_ba^b=\tfrac12n^a\partial_a(\eta(n,n))=0$ and $n_bh^{bc}=0$. Contracting with $n_b$ gives $-\big(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta\big)$ and projecting with $h$ gives the second bracket, so the two equations are equivalent to conservation. Source: the flat restriction of the perfect-fluid computation of G6 and of (4.53)-(4.55) of Tong. No choice principle is used. This argument divides by neither $\varepsilon+P$ nor $P$: the degenerate case $\varepsilon+P=0$ is retained. All quantities use at most first coordinate derivatives of the $C^1$ fields.

proposed_subjects.title: Dust stress-energy in a boosted inertial frame
proposed_subjects.statement: In an inertial frame $x$ let dust at rest have constant rest coefficient $\rho>0$, so $T^{ab}=\rho\,\delta^a_0\delta^b_0$; the only nonzero component is $T^{00}=\rho$. Consider the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along the $x^1$ axis with parameter $\beta$, $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$: $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$, $x'^2=x^2$, $x'^3=x^3$. By the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii), $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2\beta\rho,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2\beta^2\rho,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=0,$$ all remaining components zero; equivalently $T'=\rho\,n'\otimes n'$ where $n'$ is the image of $e_0$ under the boost, $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$, the future unit direction of the dust in the primed frame. The primed coordinate coefficient $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho$ is the numerical factorization $\gamma^2\rho=\gamma(\gamma\rho)$. Its source interpretation as one energy factor and one volume factor belongs to the separately adopted dust model reading; it is not an empirical identification proved by this component calculation. All primed components are constant, so $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=0$, consistently with [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. The example is a component computation; it asserts no measurement and no dynamics.
proposed_subjects.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ with the boost matrix $\Lambda$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: only $T^{00}=\rho$ contributes, giving the displayed components; the identification $T'=\rho n'\otimes n'$ follows from $n'=\Lambda e_0$. Constancy and conservation are immediate. Source: Crowell Example 5 p. 185 and (1.106) of Carroll. No choice principle is used.

proposed_subjects.title: Perfect fluid components in its rest frame and in a moving frame
proposed_subjects.statement: Let $T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$ be the perfect-fluid tensor of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]], with $n$ future unit. In an inertial frame with $n=e_0$ (fluid at rest) the components are $T^{00}=\varepsilon$, $T^{11}=T^{22}=T^{33}=P$ and all other components zero. Let $|\beta|<1$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$. Under the passive boost along $x^1$ with parameter $\beta$ (so that its primed coordinate velocity is $-\beta c\,e_1\prime$, with speed $|\beta|c$), the component law gives $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta^2+P,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=P,$$ all remaining components zero. In particular the adapted-frame numerical contraction is $T^{ab}(e_0\prime)_a(e_0\prime)_b=T\prime{}^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P$. Its difference from $\varepsilon$ is $(\gamma^2-1)(\varepsilon+P)$, so equality holds if and only if $\beta=0$ or $\varepsilon+P=0$. It is at least $\varepsilon$ whenever $\varepsilon+P\ge0$; no positivity of $\varepsilon+P$ is assumed here. The transverse diagonal components remain $P$. The computation uses the observer decomposition of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] to identify this numerical contraction; it asserts no equation of state and no measurement.
proposed_subjects.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d[(\varepsilon+P)n^cn^d+P\eta^{cd}]$ using $\eta'=\eta$ (metric preservation, [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]]) and $n'=\Lambda n$ with $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$; the displayed components follow. The adapted-frame numerical contraction is clause (c) of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] at $n=e_0'$. Source: (4.53) of Tong, (1.107)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.6 of Crowell. No choice principle is used. Subtracting $\varepsilon$ gives $(\gamma^2-1)(\varepsilon+P)$, and $\gamma^2-1=\beta^2/(1-\beta^2)$ vanishes exactly for $\beta=0$. Thus equality also holds for every boost when $\varepsilon+P=0$, and the inequality has exactly the stated conditional sign.

proposed_subjects.title: A dust solution with constant velocity and transverse density profile
proposed_subjects.statement: Let $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let $n$ be the constant field with inertial components $n^0=\gamma$, $n^1=\gamma\beta$, $n^2=n^3=0$ (so $\eta(n,n)=-1$), and let $\rho(t,x)=\rho_0(x^2,x^3)$ be a positive $C^1$ function of the transverse coordinates only. Then $n^a\partial_a\rho=\gamma(\partial_0\rho+\beta\partial_1\rho)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ because $n$ is constant, so $(\rho,n)$ satisfies the dust equations and $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$ is conserved by [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. For any finite spatial box $\bar K=[c_1,d_1]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$ whose slab lies in the chart domain, the finite slice integrals $Q^b(s)=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)d^3x$ are constant in $s$, because $T^{0b}$ is time independent. This also follows from the slice-balance identity [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b): $T^{2b}=T^{3b}=0$, and the two $x^1$-face fluxes $T^{1b}=\rho_0\gamma\beta n^b$ agree pointwise and cancel with opposite orientations. The individual $x^1$-face flux need not vanish. A nonzero transverse profile is not compactly supported in all three spatial variables, since it is independent of $x^1$. The nonnegative variant $\rho_0\ge0$, including compact support in the transverse $(x^2,x^3)$ plane, gives the same exact conserved solution and finite-box constancy, with the zero-density qualification of [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]\,(b). The flow lines are the parallel straight lines $x^1=\beta x^0+\mathrm{const}$, $x^2,x^3$ constant. The example exhibits a family of exact solutions of the dust equations; it asserts no interaction and no measurement.
proposed_subjects.strategy: Verify $\eta(n,n)=-\gamma^2+\gamma^2\beta^2=-1$. Since $n$ is constant, $\partial_an^b=0$ and $\partial_an^a=0$; since $\rho$ depends only on $x^2,x^3$, $n^a\partial_a\rho=0$. Hence both dust equations hold, including for the nonnegative-profile variant, and [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]] gives conservation. On any finite spatial box, $T^{0b}=\gamma\rho_0 n^b$ is continuous and independent of $x^0$, so its finite integral is constant. In the exact slice identity [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b), the divergence term vanishes; the $x^2,x^3$ terms vanish separately and the $x^1$ terms cancel because the integrands and their transverse integration domains are equal on both faces. Clause (c), which requires each side flux to vanish, is not used. The integral curves have constant tangent $n$, hence the stated parallel affine lines. The entire calculation uses prescribed fields and no matter-model or empirical assertion. No choice principle is used.

proposed_subjects.title: A static uniaxial stress: tension must be constant along the stressed direction
proposed_subjects.statement: In an inertial chart let $T^{ab}(x)=\rho(x^1)e_0^ae_0^b+P(x^1)e_1^ae_1^b$ with $\rho,P$ of class $C^1$ on an interval of $x^1$ (a static uniaxial stress field in the $e_1$ direction; $P<0$ is a tension). Then the balance components are $\partial_aT^{a0}=\partial_0\rho(x^1)=0$ and $\partial_aT^{a1}=\partial_1T^{11}=P'(x^1)$, so $T$ is conserved on a connected chart domain if and only if $P$ is constant there; the energy density $\rho(x^1)$ may vary while the tension must be uniform along the stressed direction. This reproduces the static equilibrium condition of a uniform rope under tension and shows that conservation constrains the stress, not the energy density, in this configuration. The example is a component computation and asserts no material model.
proposed_subjects.strategy: The components are $T^{00}=\rho(x^1)$, $T^{11}=P(x^1)$ and all others zero. Thus $\partial_aT^{a0}=\partial_0T^{00}=0$, $\partial_aT^{a1}=\partial_1T^{11}=P\prime(x^1)$, and the $b=2,3$ components vanish. In general the full tensor derivative $\partial_1(\rho e_0\otimes e_0)=\rho\prime e_0\otimes e_0$ is nonzero; it does not enter the divergence because its first tensor index is $0$. Therefore conservation is equivalent to $P\prime=0$ on the interval of $x^1$ values attained in the chart. The $x^1$ range of a connected chart domain is an interval: if an intermediate value $r$ were absent, the nonempty relatively open sets $\Omega\cap\{x^1<r\}$ and $\Omega\cap\{x^1>r\}$ would disconnect the domain. Thus on this interval and [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] makes $P$ constant there. The density profile remains unrestricted apart from its stated $C^1$ regularity. Source: Crowell Example 8 pp. 188-189 with the stated signature conversion; no material model or force law is deduced. No choice principle is used.

proposed_subjects.title: Null plane-wave scalar field and its conserved stress-energy tensor
proposed_subjects.statement: Let $k\neq0$ be a null covector, $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$, with $k^\sharp$ future, let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$, and let $\varphi(x):=f(k_ax^a+\theta_0)$ in an inertial chart; take $V\equiv0$ and $K>0$. Then $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field, $\partial_a\varphi=f'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)k_a$ and $\Box\varphi=k^ak_af''(k_ax^a+\theta_0)=0$, so $\varphi$ solves the massless scalar-field equation of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]. Its Hilbert stress-energy tensor is $$T^{ab}=Kf'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)^2\,k^ak^b,$$ symmetric; wherever $f\prime\ne0$ it is a positive multiple of the rank-one tensor $k^\sharp\otimes k^\sharp$ with future-null generating vector $k^\sharp$, and wherever $f\prime=0$ it is the zero tensor. In either case one has $T^{ab}n_an_b=Kf'^2\,(k_an^a)^2\ge0$ for every future unit observer $n$, and conserved, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, by [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solution $\Box\varphi=0$. In an inertial frame $T^{00}=Kf'^2(k^0)^2\ge0$. The example is an explicit conditional computation for the massless scalar model; it asserts no wave observation and no measurement.
proposed_subjects.strategy: Substitute $\partial_a\varphi=f'k_a$ into the Hilbert tensor formula of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]; the potential term drops and $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$ kills the trace term, leaving $Kf'^2k^ak^b$. The equation of motion holds because $k$ is null, and conservation follows from [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]]. Source: the scalar stress tensor (4.51) of Tong with V=0; the null-covector condition is the framework's own. No choice principle is used. The coefficient $Kf\prime{}^2$ is strictly positive exactly where $f\prime\ne0$ and vanishes exactly where $f\prime=0$, because $K>0$. Since $k^\sharp$ is a fixed nonzero future-null vector, this proves the precise rank-one/zero alternative. Squaring $k_an^a$ gives the nonnegative observer contraction stated without any claim that the zero tensor is future null.

before_consumer.title: Adopted continuum matter models and their evolution equations
before_consumer.statement: Adopt, on top of the flat spacetime postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], the SI conventions [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and the particle premises [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], the following classical continuum matter models on an open set $\Omega\subseteq A$: (i) Scalar field. A real smooth dimensionless field $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, a smooth potential $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with values in inverse square metres and a constant $K>0$ in joule per metre have the field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ -- the Euler-Lagrange equation of the adopted action on compactly supported variations ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]); the model's stress-energy tensor is the Hilbert tensor of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]. (ii) Dust. A $C^1$ rest energy density $\rho>0$ (joule per cubic metre) and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) satisfy $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the stress-energy tensor is $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$. (iii) Perfect fluid. $C^1$ fields $\varepsilon$ (energy density) and $P$ (pressure), both in joule per cubic metre, and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ satisfy the energy-balance and Euler equations of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; an equation of state or evolution equation determining $P$ is part of the model and is not supplied by this postulate; the stress-energy tensor is $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$. (iv) Additivity. The total stress-energy tensor of a composite system is the sum of the stress-energy tensors of its constituents (tensor-field addition on $\Omega$). This postulate adopts model equations and tensor identifications only: it does not assert conservation of the tensors (that is derived from these equations in [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]), does not select any force law, interaction, equation of state, thermodynamic or dissipative behaviour, does not claim that these models exhaust physical matter, and contains no empirical premise, measurement or uncertainty statement.
before_consumer.strategy: Adopted physical premise; no proof obligation (the schema records postulates with formulation, scope and sources, not a deduction). The mathematical content used in the formulation is confined to the model equations and the displayed tensors; conservation is deliberately NOT part of this postulate. Sources: the scalar action and equation of motion are 4.5.1 of Tong; the fluid equations are 4.5.4 of Tong and the displayed tensors are (4.53) of Tong, (1.106)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.3-9.2.6 of Crowell; the choice to adopt, rather than derive, the matter dynamics follows the source statements that conservation follows from each model's own equations of motion (Carroll p. 30) and that matter actions and equations of state are separate model assumptions (Tong 4.5). No empirical support is claimed.

before_consumer.title: Local conservation of stress-energy for the adopted matter models
before_consumer.statement: Under the matter premises of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]: (a) If $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field solving the adopted field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$, then the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]) satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$, in every inertial chart. (b) If $\rho>0$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted dust equations, then $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely if $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ and $\rho>0$ then the dust equations hold. (c) If $\varepsilon,P$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted fluid equations, then $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely conservation of that $T$ implies the two fluid equations. (d) For a $C^1$ symmetric tensor field prescribed on $\Omega$ that is not obtained from one of the adopted models together with its field equations, no conservation is asserted; a conservation statement about such a field is an additional explicit premise. (e) The theorem is a conditional deduction from the adopted model equations; it asserts no interaction, force law, cross section, measurement or empirical fact, and its conclusions inherit the scope of the postulate.
before_consumer.strategy: Clause (a) is [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solutions of the adopted field equation; clause (b) is [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]; clause (c) is [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]. Clause (d) records the absence of any derivation for arbitrary prescribed tensors: the local balance $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$ of [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]] is a definition, and no hypothesis in this page forces $f=0$ for an arbitrary $T$. Clause (e) restates the physical scope. No empirical premise is used and the conclusion carries no measurement interpretation.

before_consumer.title: Perfect fluid components in its rest frame and in a moving frame
before_consumer.statement: Let $T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$ be the perfect-fluid tensor of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]], with $n$ future unit. In an inertial frame with $n=e_0$ (fluid at rest) the components are $T^{00}=\varepsilon$, $T^{11}=T^{22}=T^{33}=P$ and all other components zero. Under the passive boost along $x^1$ with parameter $\beta$ (so that in the primed frame the fluid moves with speed $v=\beta c$ in the negative $x'^1$ direction), the component law gives $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta^2+P,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=P,$$ all remaining components zero. In particular the observer at rest in the primed frame measures the energy density $T'(e_0',e_0')=T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P$, which differs from the rest-frame density $\varepsilon$ unless $\beta=0$ and is at least $\varepsilon$ when $\varepsilon+P\ge0$; the transverse diagonal components stay equal to the pressure $P$. The computation uses the observer decomposition of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] to read $T'^{00}$ as an energy density; it asserts no equation of state and no measurement.
before_consumer.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d[(\varepsilon+P)n^cn^d+P\eta^{cd}]$ using $\eta'=\eta$ (metric preservation, [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]]) and $n'=\Lambda n$ with $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$; the displayed components follow. The energy-density reading is clause (c) of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] at $n=e_0'$. Source: (4.53) of Tong, (1.107)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.6 of Crowell. No choice principle is used.

before_consumer.title: Adopted total stress-energy and isolation premise for integrated conservation
before_consumer.statement: Adopt as the boundary and isolation premise of the continuum framework: (i) Total tensor. In every conservation or integration statement of this framework the tensor used is the total stress-energy tensor of the system considered, including every constituent that carries energy-momentum -- matter, fields and supporting structures present in the region -- assembled by the additivity clause of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]. (ii) Localisation. Whenever conservation of a slice four-momentum over a coordinate-time interval $[s_1,s_2]$ is asserted in an inertial chart, the model assumes that during that interval the total tensor is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of a closed box $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$, that its components satisfy the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces of the box for $i=1,2,3$, and that the slice integrals converge; equivalently, the system is isolated inside the chosen region for the chosen interval. (iii) Failure of isolation. If the side flux does not vanish, only the exact finite-flux balance of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] is asserted; no conservation of a slice integral is inferred and no limiting procedure at spatial infinity is adopted. (iv) Unmodelled matter. For a matter system not governed by one of the models of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]], conservation of its stress-energy tensor is not inferred; if used it must be adopted or derived separately. (v) Exclusion caution. Removing a constituent -- a support, a field or a container -- from the total tensor can make the side-flux condition fail; the premise concerns the total tensor of the system, not an arbitrary partial tensor. This premise is an idealisation of an isolated bounded system in flat spacetime; it is not a measurement and makes no apparatus, statistical or empirical claim.
before_consumer.strategy: Adopted physical premise; no proof obligation. The zero-flux condition is exactly the hypothesis of the mathematical finite-flux theorem [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(c), so the premise is stated in the form the deduction consumes. Sources: the isolation/vacuum-side argument is 9.3.4 of Crowell pp. 195-197; the flat conserved-charge box argument is 4.5.5 of Tong, including the warning that one must require vanishing current on the timelike boundary; the container/support caution is the reader-recorded defect discussion of Crowell pp. 101-103 and 233-234. No measurement is reported and no empirical claim is made.

before_consumer.title: Integrated four-momentum of an isolated system on finite slices
before_consumer.statement: Let $x$ be an inertial chart, let $\bar K$ be a closed spatial box and $s_1<s_2$, and let $T$ be the total stress-energy tensor of a system in the situation of [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]]: $T$ is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$, satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ there (for the adopted models this is the conclusion of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]; for any other system it is an explicit premise), and satisfies the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces for $i=1,2,3$. Put $Q^b(s):=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ and $P^b:=Q^b/c$. Then: (a) $Q^b(s)$ is finite for every $s\in[s_1,s_2]$ and $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$; (b) consequently $P^b$ is independent of $s\in[s_1,s_2]$; if $P$ is future timelike, its invariant mass $\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$ is independent of $s$ as well; (c) if the side flux does not vanish, the exact balance is the finite-flux identity of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]], and no conservation is asserted; (d) no transformation law for $P^b$ under a change of inertial chart or slicing is asserted: without an admissible-region flux argument, $P^b$ is a chart-component integral and is not claimed to be a four-vector; no noncompact, asymptotic or gravitational-energy statement is made, and the reading of $P^b$ as the system's four-momentum is the model's interpretation of the integral, not a measurement.
before_consumer.strategy: Clause (a) applies [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(c) to the box $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$ under the measured hypotheses (conservation and vanishing side flux); the invariance of the invariant mass in (b) is immediate because $P$ is a constant future timelike vector and $\eta(P,P)$ is then constant, using the invariant-mass formula of [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]. Clause (c) is the general balance case of the same theorem. Clause (d) records the exact scope: the theorem proves constancy of the chart integrals and nothing about their transformation under a change of chart, which would require the oriented hypersurface flux construction; no noncompact limit is taken. No empirical premise is used.

before_consumer.title: Scope of the page: two notions of force, conditional conservation and excluded claims
before_consumer.statement: The force vocabulary of this framework has two distinct mathematical carriers: the four-force $F=\dot P=dP/d\tau$ on a massive particle worldline ([[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]]; its identities are conditional on [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]) and the four-force density $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ of the continuum ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Neither is a force law. The page's conservation statements are conditional deductions: local conservation of the scalar, dust and fluid tensors is proved from the adopted model equations ([[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]), while for any other matter the conservation of $T$ must be adopted separately. Integrated conservation additionally requires the isolation premise ([[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]]) and is asserted only for finite boxes and slices in one inertial chart ([[pthm-sr-integrated-conservation-for-isolated-matter]]). The framework contains no gravity, no electromagnetic coupling, no derivation of an equation of state, no energy conditions (the printed dominant-energy-condition inequality of the Crowell source p. 191 is defective and is not used), no angular-momentum theorem and no empirical premise; no measurement, apparatus or uncertainty claim is made anywhere on this page.
before_consumer.strategy: Scope remark; no proof obligation. It records which page claims are adopted premises, which are conditional deductions, and which promised or source-adjacent topics are deliberately not asserted (energy conditions, angular momentum, gravity, electromagnetism, equations of state, asymptotic charges, four-vector transformation of chart integrals). Sources: the errata and scope findings of the Crowell reader report (printed p. 191 defective DEC; pp. 231, 240 field-stress caveats) and the conservation caveats of Tong 4.5.3 and Carroll p. 30 / pp. 138-139.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of [[lem-sign-preservation-near-a-limit]] applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]].

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex ([[def-interval]]) and let
$f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$ ([[def-continuity-real]]) and
differentiable at every point of $I$ that is interior to $I$
([[def-interior-closure-boundary-r]], [[def-derivative]]), with

$$f'(x) = 0 \qquad \text{at every interior point } x \text{ of } I .$$

Then $f$ is constant on $I$: there is a real $k$ with $f(x) = k$ for every
$x \in I$.

Consequently, if $f, g : I \to \mathbb{R}$ are both continuous on $I$ and both
differentiable at every interior point of $I$, with $f'(x) = g'(x)$ at every
interior point $x$, then there is a real $k$ with

$$f(x) \;=\; g(x) + k \qquad \text{for every } x \in I .$$

**Order-convexity of $I$ is essential and is not a convenience.** The
conclusion is false on a domain that falls into separate pieces, since a
function may be constant on each piece with different constants; nothing in the
proof would survive, because the mean value theorem is applied to the segment
joining two points of the domain and that segment must lie in the domain.

**The hypothesis is imposed only at interior points.** At an endpoint of $I$
nothing is asked at all: $f$ need not be differentiable there, and the proof
never evaluates a difference quotient at an endpoint, since it applies the mean
value theorem on a segment $[u,v] \subseteq I$ and uses the derivative only at
points of $(u,v)$, all of which are interior to $I$. What is *not* meant is that
the derivative at an endpoint is free to be nonzero: once $f$ is known to be
constant its difference quotient at an endpoint is constantly $0$, so wherever
$f'$ exists at an endpoint it is $0$ too. That is a consequence of the theorem,
not a hypothesis of it.

Let $a \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a > 0$ and let $r \in \mathbb{Q}$ ([[def-rationals]]).

Every rational has a representative with positive denominator
([[lem-rat-positive-denominator]]), so write $r = m/n$ with $m \in \mathbb{Z}$
and $n$ a positive integer; a positive integer is the image of a unique natural
$\ge 1$ ([[lem-nat-embeds-int]]), and we write $n$ for that natural too. Define

$$a^{r} := \big(a^{1/n}\big)^{m},$$

where $a^{1/n}$ is the unique nonnegative $n$-th root of $a$
([[thm-nth-roots-exist]]) and the outer exponent is an integer power
([[def-integer-power]]). The outer power is legitimate because $a^{1/n} > 0$ when
$a > 0$, so it has an inverse and negative integer exponents are allowed.

**Well-definedness.** The right-hand side must not depend on which representative
$m/n$ of $r$ was chosen. It does not: that is [[lem-rational-power-well-defined]],
which is recorded in this item's `justified_by` rather than in its `deps`, since
it is a statement *about* the operation defined here and therefore depends on
this definition.

**The base must be positive.** For $a < 0$ the same formula is not a definition
at all, because different representatives of the same rational give different
answers, or no answer: see [[fs-rational-power-of-negative-base]], which is
exactly the item that justifies the restriction.

**Supplementary clause for the base $0$.** For $a = 0$ and rational $r > 0$
([[def-rat-order]]) the displayed formula still makes sense and still does not
depend on the representative: $r > 0$ forces $m \ge 1$, and
$\big(0^{1/n}\big)^{m} = 0^{m} = 0$ ([[thm-nth-roots-exist]] applies to every
$a \ge 0$). So we set $0^{r} = 0$ for rational $r > 0$. For $r < 0$ the
expression $0^{r}$ is left undefined, since $0$ has no inverse. This clause is
what lets the inequalities later on this page be stated for nonnegative entries
rather than for positive ones only.

For every smooth compactly supported $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ define the first variation $$\delta S(\varphi)[h]:=-\frac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\Big(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_bh+V'(\varphi)h\Big)\,d^4x,$$ a finite Riemann integral by compact support of $h$ ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(c)). The equation in (b) is called the scalar-field equation of this model. The statement is the first variation of the action on compactly supported variations; it asserts nothing about convergence of $S$ on unbounded domains, no boundary term, no dynamics beyond the equivalence in (b) and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used.

supplier_registry.exact_interface: Let (V,eta) be a Lorentz vector space and let T := {v in V : eta(v,v) < 0} be its timelike set. By the components lemma T has exactly two connected components; a time orientation of (V,eta) is a choice of one of them. Fixing such a choice and writing C^+ for the chosen component and C^- := T \ C^+ for the other, call v future timelike if v is in C^+, past timelike if v is in C^-, future null if v is nonzero, eta(v,v) = 0 and v lies in the closure cl(C^+), past null if v is nonzero, eta(v,v) = 0 and v lies in cl(C^-), future causal if it is future timelike or future null, and past causal if it is past timelike or past null. The sets cl(C^+) and cl(C^-) are the future and past closed cones; they are convex cones meeting only at 0, and a causal vector is future or past but not both.
